newsitem.title: JAPAN: Beckett says Labour won't be indecisive on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Beckett says Labour won't be indecisive on EMU.

text.p: Britain's new trade chief Margaret Beckett said in Tokyo on Tuesday the Labour government would not be indecisive about whether to join a single European currency.
Without giving a hint of what Labour's decision would be on European economic and monetary union (EMU), Beckett said there would be no hesitation once the choice was made.

Portraying previous Conservative governments as "drifting" on the EMU issue, Beckett said Labour would make its decision at the appropriate time solely on the basis of where Britain's best interests lay.
"If Britain intends going in, we'll go in," she said in a speech to the British Chamber of Commerce in Tokyo.
Beckett, secretary of trade and industry, is making her first foreign visit since Labour's general election victory.
Her main aim is to assure Japanese businesses that Labour does not plan any policy changes that would threaten their strategy of using Britain as a gateway into Europe.
